answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake that unlocks only after a slow, glacier-like vesting period: new agents earn trust gradually by completing verified work, and each fake identity an attacker spawns must lock the same stake and wait the same long thaw. One fraud sends a ripple through the whole cluster — linked identities forfeit their stakes together — so spinning up ten thousand sock puppets costs ten thousand stakes, while a single honest lantern of reputation, built over months of real service, stays cheap to keep and expensive to fake.
